output.summary: KEP-3962 proposes mutating admission policies declared in CEL, as an alternative to mutating admission webhooks, building on the validating admission policy work in KEP-3488. The KEP is recorded as implemented and at stable stage, with implementable status from 2024-02-08 and implemented status from 2026-05-21.
output.rationale:
Simple mutations such as setting a label, setting a field, or adding a sidecar container can be expressed in a few lines of CEL, avoiding the complexity of a webhook. CEL mutations let the apiserver introspect which fields are read and written, and in-process mutation is fast enough to re-run policies. The design combines CEL object instantiation with JSON Patch and Server Side Apply merge algorithms.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Typed object initializer similar to Go (e.g. core.v1.pod) in CEL
alternatives.why_not: The KEP notes this will not work for multiple resources matched.

alternatives.option: Use a plain map directly in CEL
alternatives.why_not: The KEP notes this makes type checking hard.

alternatives.option: Plain YAML-style patch syntax without type declarations
alternatives.why_not: Commenters judged it would be equivalent to a new language in itself if conditionals and similar features were added; the KEP does not adopt it.

evidence.quote: This enhancement adds mutating admission policies, declared using CEL expressions, as an alternative to mutating admission webhooks.
A large proportion of mutating admission needs are for relatively simple operations such as setting a label, setting a field, or adding a sidecar container to a pod.

With updates for different mutation type options as alpha, protection for atomic lists, and re-using the selection and binding strategy from validating admission policy, I'm comfortable with proceeding on this KEP.
A replacement KEP for this is in the works by @cici37. Closing this one.
